points.description: States that the array length can be specified in the array declaration, i.e. explicitly giving the size in square brackets (e.g. int a[5];).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only vaguely 'when declaring' without clearly saying the size is given in the declaration brackets.

points.description: States that the array length can be specified by using an initializer list, i.e. the size is deduced from the number of values in the braces (e.g. int a[] = {1,2,3};).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if it mentions initializing with values/braces but does not say the length comes from the initializer list.

rubric.notes: Both ways are required: (1) size given in the array declaration and (2) size determined by an initializer list. Each way must be stated precisely; vague answers such as 'when creating it' or 'with values' earn nothing or at most half. Naming a wrong way (e.g. dynamic allocation with new, or sizeof) as one of the two costs that point.
